title: Networks and data centers
summary: Cluster networks, rack power and the energy of every token.

links.why: rare errors become daily at fleet scale
links.if: a fleet grows to millions of chips
links.then: errors that are one in a million happen every day

links.if: AI needs power faster than grids can add it
links.then: AI growth slows in many futures

links.why: racks are only as fast as their memory

ideas.how: HBM and fast networks exist so data arrives in time
one model is split across thousands of chips joined by fast networks
power and cooling limit how many chips a site can run

tradeoffs.how: serving answers faster costs more energy per token

measures.how: energy per token is the same idea, for a whole data center
memory and networks both have to keep up

then: Computing lives in mainframes, minicomputers and PCs.
Web companies build large data centers from ordinary PC servers.
Cloud computing (from 2006) puts servers in giant shared data centers.
GPU clusters linked by NVLink (from 2016) and fast networks train AI models.

challenges.title: What does power really cost AI?
challenges.task: Double the price of electricity on the map and see how far the cost of an AI answer moves.

learn.plain: An AI chip is like a giant factory that needs constant deliveries. Memory chips are the warehouses next door, the network is the road system between factories, and the power plant keeps the lights on. If any of them can't keep up, the factory sits idle.
learn.engineer: Scale-up fabrics (NVLink 6 at 3.6 TB/s per GPU) versus scale-out at 1.6 Tb/s per GPU shape parallelism; optics power and PUE shape joules per token.

options: Total facility power divided by the power used by the IT equipment
quiz.why: A PUE of 1.2 means 20% extra power for cooling and conversion losses.
